correctness.rationale: For every fixed radius on a path, the ball average of a nondecreasing sequence is nondecreasing as the center moves right: the ball either shifts right, appends a new largest value, removes an old smallest value, or is unchanged. The pointwise maximum over radii is therefore nondecreasing. Its left endpoint is the global mean and its right endpoint is the terminal value, so total variation telescopes to the stated exact formula. The mean is bounded below by \(((n-1)f(1)+f(n))/n\), yielding the factor \((n-1)/n\) with equality exactly when all intermediate values equal the lower endpoint. Reflection proves the nonincreasing case. An exact-rational finite verifier confirms the formulas and equality cases on all monotone integer sequences of lengths \(3\) through \(8\) with values in \(\{0,1,2,3\}\); this computation is supplementary, not the infinite proof.
